annotationRationale: The increasing-then-decreasing structure gives a bijection between fair numbers and chosen digit sets with left-or-right assignments. Combinations select the digits, the multiplication principle counts assignments, and the binomial theorem sums over lengths.
sourceMethod: Follows the official count by length: choose the digits, assign smaller digits to either side of the maximum, and sum with the binomial theorem. The structural justification and uniqueness of the encoding are made explicit.

review.mathCheck: With distinct digits, any decrease followed by an increase creates a forbidden local minimum. Thus each chosen k-digit set has exactly 2^(k−1) fair arrangements, including empty sides and k=1. Summing gives (3^9−1)/2=9841, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Problem 24: characterize the single peak, choose the digits and their sides, then apply the binomial theorem. The inverse encoding explicitly prevents omissions and duplicates.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed bijection, combinations and binomial theorem are central; multiplication is appropriate supporting knowledge. No material omission.
